STEP 1 - Scene: A small snack of red grapes on a white square plate, photographed from above at a near-top-down angle. Only the grapes are visible; no other food on this plate.

STEP 2 - Ruler: The plate is a square-ish white plate about 20 cm across (side-plate size). Radius ~10 cm, but the plate is square-cornered, so I use roughly 20 x 20 cm = 400 cm^2 as the vessel area, a reasonable estimate.

STEP 3 - Items: Red seedless grapes, about 15 visible, one small stem.

STEP 4 - Area: The grape cluster covers roughly 12% of the plate area (about 48 cm^2). The rest is empty plate.

STEP 5 - Volume: Grapes form a cluster about 2 cm deep on average. 48 cm^2 x 2 cm = ~96 ml gross volume.

STEP 6 - Grams: Grapes are fruit pieces, bulk density ~0.6 g/ml. 96 ml x 0.6 = ~58 g.

STEP 7 - Energy: Red grapes ~69 kcal per 100 g. 58 g x 0.69 = ~40 kcal.

STEP 8 - Sanity check: About 15 grapes weigh roughly 50–60 g, which matches typical grape weight (~4 g each). About 40 kcal is plausible for a small handful of grapes.
